feed.subtitle: Dr. Pramiti Sarker, Ph.D., AEP, conducts research aimed at improving workplace ergonomics to enhance employees' well-being. Her research focuses on optimizing performance and mitigating workers’ physical and cognitive workload to prevent neuromusculoskeletal disorders, improve job quality, and support sustainable careers. Excessive workload can reduce worker performance and increase employer costs. She identifies workload strain sources and develops, evaluates, and implements ergonomic interventions that reduce risk and enhance overall well-being. Before joining West Virginia University, she served as a Visiting Assistant Professor at the Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering at Purdue University, a Lecturer at the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), and completed an internship at the Mayo Clinic. Education: Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering, Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering, Ames, Iowa, USA, 2022. M.S. in Industrial Engineering, Department of Industrial and Production Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), Dhaka, Bangladesh, 2017. B.S. in Industrial Engineering, Department of Industrial and Production Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), Dhaka, Bangladesh, 2015.
